ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior officers against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) PEP list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean government's own sanctions list. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, including verification of source of funds and wealth, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a real-time basis for new sanctions designations, and at least annually. All results must be documented and retained for at least five years. Failure to screen adequately may result in criminal penalties and revocation of the GDP license.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Online (Internet Registration Service - IROS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be registered in Korean script (Hangul), but may include English or other foreign words if transliterated into Hangul. The name must be distinguishable from existing registered names and must not be identical or confusingly similar. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a unique name, (2) a description of the business purpose, (3) the legal form 'Chusik Hoesa' (stock corporation), and (4) no prohibited or sensitive tokens. English names may be used as a secondary name but must be transliterated for registration.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: As of the current Korean Commercial Act, no statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a general Chusik Hoesa that is not a bank, financial investment business, insurance company, or other regulated financial institution. However, the entire amount of issued share subscription money must be paid in before registration and held in a blocked temporary escrow account in the name of the promoter or the notary until the incorporation registration is completed, after which funds may be released for lawful corporate use. The Articles of Incorporation may impose a higher internal paid-in capital threshold based on the Company's GDP clinical logistics business plan.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [PHARMA LOGISTICS HOLDINGS] CHUSIK HOESA. The directors of [PHARMA LOGISTICS HOLDINGS] Chusik Hoesa (the 'Company') met formally at the registered office set forth in the Articles of Incorporation on [Date], at [Time], for the first meeting of the Board of Directors. It was announced that notice of the meeting had been waived by all directors and that a quorum was present, and the chairperson declared the meeting duly constituted in accordance with Article 390 of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea. That the registered office of the Company shall be and hereby is adopted as [Address], within the jurisdiction of the competent District Court, and the representative director is authorized to execute and file the registered office lease, business registration, and all public licensing documents. 3. That the following statutory officers are appointed: [Name] as Representative Director (Dae-pyo), [Name] as Chief Financial Officer and officer responsible for books and records, and [Name] as compliance officer for GDP and pharmaceutical regulatory affairs, each to serve until the next ordinary general meeting of shareholders or until earlier removal. 4. That the Representative Director, the Chief Financial Officer and any two joint signatories, particularly [Name], are authorized in the name of the Company to open, operate and close bank accounts at [Bank], to negotiate and execute deposit or loan documents with any bank in Korea, to issue deposit certificates, to sign checks, to make SWIFT wire transfers and direct ACH payments, and to execute guarantees as approved by the Board. 5. That the Representative Director is authorized to apply for all governmental permits, including the general business registration at the National Tax Service, GDP compliance certification from the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, freight forwarding registration, Civil Defense fire permits, occupational safety clearances, and customs or bonded storage permissions. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be recorded in the corporate minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public appointed under the Framework Act on Notarial Acts and the Ministry of Justice, with subsequent registration support via the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, stating the Company name ending in Chusik Hoesa, the precise registered office in Korea, the corporate purpose limited to certified GDP pharmaceutical freight and cold-chain logistics, authorized share capital, issued shares, transfer restrictions if any, method of contribution, number of directors, auditors or inspector requirements, fiscal year, reserve funds, and general meeting rules. Verify the proposed corporate name through the Supreme Court corporate registration name search to avoid identical or confusing names. Obtain identity documents, passports, lease agreements, and founder statements confirming lawful permissive use of the registered office address. Appear before the notary public, confirm the promoters' identities and lawful capacity, declare the paid-in capital subscription, and execute the Articles of Incorporation. The notary must verify the legality of the corporate purpose, the subscription method, and the escrow deposit arrangement, then authenticate the Articles. After notarization, transmit or deliver the notarized instrument to the corporate registration counsel for filing at the competent District Court.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of each promoter
Power of attorney for the incorporating agent or attorney
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Proof of registered office address (lease certificate or certified title, landlord consent form)
Founder statement of identity and lawful capacity
Paid-in capital escrow deposit confirmation or bank receipt
Certificate of corporate name search result
Notarization fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses authentication, correct any signature, address, capacity, or corporate-object defect shown in the refusal letter, re-notarize within three days, and amend the Articles if the notary identifies a legal incompatibility. If the corporate name search is disputed by a comparable prior registration, select a new exclusive name and restart the notarial execution with the revised Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration of the Chusik Hoesa with the Competent District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court or the District Court having exclusive jurisdiction over the Company's registered office, through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office or in-person filing window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal corporation registration application to the competent District Court within two weeks of notarization, identifying the newly notarized Articles of Incorporation, the paid escrow receipt, proof of paid-in capital, directors' appointments, registered office, and corporate objects. Pay the statutorily prescribed state registration fee and education surtax online or at the court cashier. The reviewing registry officer verifies compliance with Commercial Act Articles 288, 289, 291, 295, and 318; checks that the registered office is a genuine physical address; verifies the paid-in capital deposit; and confirms that the promoters' names and share subscriptions are consistent with the notarial record. Once the registration is accepted, the court issues a certificate of corporate registration and a corporate seal registration may then be established at the same authority. The representative director should collect the final registration certificate, certified extract of enrollment, and corporate seal certificate which will be the legal proof of the Company's existence for banking, tax, and license applications.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Application form for corporation registration
Paid-in capital escrow deposit certificate
Founders' passport copies
Landlord identification and consent for registered office
Corporate name search certificate
Council reporting record of directors
Power of attorney authorizing the submitting agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order, revise the Articles or corroborating evidence and resubmit within the court-set correction period, typically 14 days. If the registration is suspended due to an address dispute, submit a revised lease or acquisition document proving lawful occupancy. If the name conflict arises, choose a new name and apply anew. If the examiner questions the paid-in capital, deliver the bank escrow ledger or notarial paid-in capital certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Social Insurance, and Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Hannuri local District Tax Office for the registered office jurisdiction, and the automatic linkage with the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Employment Insurance, and Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 60 days after corporate registration, the Representative Director must apply for business registration with the authority of the registered office located tax office and obtain a business registration certificate, corporate tax number, and registered corporate tax invoice issuance ID. This step also establishes the Company as a VAT taxable business and generates the electronic tax invoice ledger. Bimonthly VAT returns, annual corporate tax declarations, payroll withholding for employees, and dividend withholding tax on any shareholder distributions will then become due under the Tax Act. The same representative director shall complete the four mandatory social insurance registrations through the Ministry of Employment and Labor and the relevant insurance agencies so that employees are covered for pension, health, employment, and industrial accident compensation. This step also produces the banking KYC package expected by Swift Wire and Direct ACH payment intermediaries, including the corporate registration certificate, tax registration certificate, director identification, and a corporate bank account. The registered office lease and the commercial register extract are attached to the business registration filing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration issued by the court
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Representative director identification and passport copy
Business registration application form
Registered office lease or title document
Power of attorney if filed by agent
Board resolution appointing the representative director
Corporate seal certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS queries the application, correct the business category code, address proof, or director identity gaps and resubmit through the Hannuri website within 10 days. If the registered office is unable to receive mail, change the address and notify the NTS before the business registration is finalized. If the four social insurance registrations are rejected or incompletely linked, present the corporate registration extract to the relevant offices or use the unified online claim service. If a tax audit pre-assessment blocks VAT registration, cooperate with the tax officer, file the explanatory documents, and seek correction through the director's oral response within 20 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory GDP, Freight Forwarding, Fire Safety, and Workplace Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) Good Distribution Practice Assessment Team; Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport Freight Logistics Policy Division; local Fire Station under the National Fire Agency; Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency; and the Korea Customs Service if a bonded warehouse or customs cargo storage licence is required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to MFDS for the Good Distribution Practice (GDP) certification covering the Company's pharmaceutical logistics and clinical freight operations. Prepare and submit the quality manual, standard operating procedures for receiving, storage, dispatch, temperature excursion, returns, recalls, and falsified medicines; conduct a full temperature mapping study of all cold-chain storage areas and vehicles; validate data loggers; submit the staff training records, self-audit reports, supplier qualification documents, and pharmacovigilance contact agreement. During MFDS inspection, demonstrate historical traceability and quarantine of nonconforming products. Simultaneously, submit the freight forwarding registration to the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport if acting as a freight forwarder or customs broker. Apply to the local Fire Station for a Fire Safety Certificate covering the building's installed extinguishing, alarm, evacuation, and emergency lighting systems; obtain the National Fire Agency's completed inspection certificate. Register with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency and complete the workplace safety and health improvement plan if warehousing staff operate forklifts, racking, or mechanically moved cargo. If goods will be stored under customs control, apply to the Korea Customs Service for bonded warehouse approval. Receive the final GDP certificate, operating licence and civil defense fire inspection certificate before commercial operations.
required_dossiers: MFDS GDP application form
Quality management manual and SOPs
Temperature mapping validation reports for cold stores and vehicles
Staff training records and organisational chart
Warehouse layout plan with zoning, quarantine, and returned goods areas
Dangerous goods or hazardous pharmaceutical waste handling procedure
Fire protection system completion documents and structural drawings
Freight forwarding registration application and ETA/ETD process flow
Insurance coverage certificate and industrial compensation registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MFDS pauses the GDP review, submit a corrective and preventive action plan with revised SOPs and temperature mapping evidence within 30 days. If the fire service rejects the certificate, remediate the detected fire protection deficiencies and request re-inspection. If the freight forwarding registration is refused, appeal through the responsible Ministry after submitting an updated license-by-authority opinion, or present revised corporate purpose and financial capacity evidence. If the bonded warehouse license is delayed, temporarily use a third-party licensed bonded warehouse while the application is cured.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) Pharmaceutical Logistics and Supply Chain Division; Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport Freight Logistics Policy Division; local Fire Station of the National Fire Agency; Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency; and the Korea Customs Service for bonded or transit storage approval.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Pharmaceutical Good Distribution Practice (GDP) Certification for Logistic Service Providers; Freight Forwarding Business Registration; Customs Broker or Bonded Cargo Warehouse License (where applicable); and Fire Safety Operation Permit for Warehousing and Cold-Chain Facilities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, assisted operationally by the Korea Environment Corporation and local EIA supporting authorities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: The GDP clinical pharmaceutical freight and logistics scope, absent new manufacturing or chemical processing, is classified as Environmental Registration (Low-tier Registration) rather than Full EIA Report; it is exempt from a Strategic Environmental Impact Assessment only if the project site does not contain newly created land over 5,000 square metres, does not create sewage/output volume requiring public treatment works, and does not store hazardous chemicals above the Dangerous Chemicals Act thresholds. For any new building construction, a preliminary Site Land Suitability Assessment and small-scale 'Environmental Impact Assessment Support System' review may be required. For leased existing warehouses, only wastewater discharge connection permission and a waste registration declaration are required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For any sanitary or cooling water discharge, the facility shall meet Republic of Korea Water Environment Conservation Act point-source effluent standards, including BOD below 30 mg/L, COD below 40 mg/L, suspended solids below 35 mg/L, total nitrogen below 20 mg/L, and total phosphorus below 2 mg/L, or otherwise comply with local sewer authority assimilation standards set by the municipality. Volatile organic compound (VOC) fugitive emissions from cleaning agents and refrigerant systems shall not exceed the Clean Air Conservation Act threshold of 15 ppm total hydrocarbon expression, and cooling equipment shall use non-ozone-depleting refrigerants. Hazardous pharmaceutical waste, returned medicines, and expired clinical trial materials are subject to the Waste Control Act manifest system and must be disposed of solely through a licensed hazardous waste transporter under a registered hazardous waste consignment programme. Spill-containment bunkers and refrigerant leak detectors are required in all cold-chain areas.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Completion Inspection Certificate issued by the local Fire Station under the Fire Services Act, certifying that the fire alarm, extinguishing systems, emergency lighting, evacuation routes, fire doors, and smoke-control systems comply with the fire resistance standards applicable to warehouse and logistics facilities. A structural load inspection certificate for racking systems and refrigerated cold cells must be issued by a licensed structural engineer. Occupational safety and health clearance from the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency is required for forklift traffic, load bearing, electrical safety, worker exposure to cold environments, and emergency response arrangements; the Company shall also register with the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service for industrial accident compensation along with the four mandatory social insurance plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online portal: Home Tax Service (HTS) at https://www.hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign non-resident entities must apply for a Business Registration Number (BRN) at the local district Tax Office under the NTS. Required documents include: certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, proof of foreign registration, and a domestic address for tax purposes. The application can be submitted online via HTS or in person. Upon approval, the entity receives a 10-digit BRN which serves as both corporate tax ID and VAT registration number. For VAT purposes, registration is mandatory upon commencement of any business activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None – South Korea does not provide check-the-box elections; all domestic corporations are subject to entity-level corporate income tax and VAT.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No statutory threshold – mandatory registration for any business activity (KRW 0).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoices (e-invoices) for all VAT-registered businesses. E-invoices must be issued via NTS-approved systems and transmitted to NTS within 1 day after issuance. Real-time clearance and anti-fraud measures include digital signature, validation, and integration with NTS's Home Tax Service.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and certain international services are zero-rated under the VAT Act. For GDP pharma freight, zero-rating applies if the services are directly related to the export of goods (e.g., freight forwarding, customs clearance, and warehousing for export). The service provider must retain evidence of the export transaction.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties for fraudulent or unverified export zero-rating include additional tax of 40% of the claimed amount, criminal charges, and retrospective clawback of zero-rated benefits. The NTS conducts rigorous audits and cross-checks with customs data.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as central bank and foreign exchange policy executor, operating under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Ministry of Economy and Finance's delegated foreign exchange administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a negative-list foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is fully convertible for legitimate current-account payments such as freight charges, logistics service fees, royalties and other service income, provided the transaction is reported through a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank using the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). Capital-account operations, including inbound foreign direct investment, equity contributions and shareholder loans, are generally permissible but require preliminary notification/reporting under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act to KOTRA or the Ministry of Economy and Finance and must be booked through a Korean foreign exchange bank. Repatriation of profits, programme revenue and dividends to foreign shareholders is lawful once the Korean entity has satisfied corporate income tax, withholding tax, statutory audit and shareholder-meeting requirements. There is no blanket pre-approval by the Bank of Korea for routine trade-related payments in the goods-distribution and freight sector, but payment execution can be delayed if the bank identifies inconsistencies among the underlying transport contract, tax invoice, customs declaration and FEIS purpose code. In practice, non-financial barriers such as ultimate beneficial owner documentation and cross-border invoice authenticity generate more friction than legal convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: South Korea does not impose a fixed statutory surrender ratio or mandatory conversion of export foreign currency proceeds to Korean won. Export settlement, however, must be made to a domestic foreign exchange bank, and the Korean exporter is required to collect export proceeds within the credit terms specified in the trade contract, subject to a statutory outer limit of 180 days from the export declaration date unless an extension is approved by the Korea Customs Service or the Bank of Korea under FEIS rules. Proceeds may be held in a Foreign Currency Deposit Account or sold at market rate. No central bank surrender percentage applies, but all export proceeds must be traceable through the bank's FEIS report.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Foreign Currency Deposit Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Export Proceeds Deposit Account
Corporate Current Account / Foreign Currency Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally non-viable as a primary corporate clearing rail. Offshore digital EMI platforms are not foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and cannot lawfully buy or sell Korean won with residents, hold resident corporate operating accounts, or issue FEIS reports to Korean authorities. They may be used by the foreign parent or non-resident supplier side as convenience deposit accounts, but the Korean Chusik Hoesa must maintain its revenue, capital escrow, FX purchase/sale and trade settlement through a domestic Tier-1 Korean bank. Relying on an EMI for outbound KRW or trade settlement would create KYC discontinuities and invalid proof-of-payment records for Korean tax and customs clearance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical branch appearance is mandatory, in principle, for at least one statutory director and the authorized Korean resident representative when opening a corporate account for a foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa. Remote consular proxy opening alone is not accepted by most Korean banks; the bank compliance committee requires a face-to-face interview with the principal director or a Korean-resident director with board resolution authority. Supplementary directors abroad may execute a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, and a remote video KYC interview may be used to verify identity, but the final account activation is conditional on the branch's independent call-back verification and the physical document inspection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership cannot be demonstrated because the Korean entity is held through a non-resident intermediate company with an opaque ownership chain and nominee-appointed directors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified statutory extracts from the company registry; chronological share transfer ledger; notarized UBO declarations of all natural persons holding at least 10 percent of equity or control; nominee-waiver declarations; an external AML legal opinion listing the economic ownership chain; audited financial statements of the intermediate entity for the last two years; and six months of source-of-funds bank statements from the account actually remitting the capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The freight and logistics payment flows identify sanctioned vessels, transshipment in high-risk port zones, or conflicting consignee and shipper addresses in the GDP distribution route.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive OFAC, EU, UN and Korean sanctions screening results for each counterparty and transport operator; actual shipping documents including airway bill, bill of lading, CMR and packing list with complete chain of custody; route deviation explanation letter from the freight forwarder; customs cargo declarations; temperature-controlled GDP monitoring records; cargo insurance policy; and a certificate from the responsible GDP officer confirming that the pharmaceutical cargo was not diverted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Invoice valuation in the pharmaceutical freight transactions appears under-priced relative to benchmark temperature-controlled logistics rates, raising trade-based money laundering exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Benchmark rate analysis from an independent freight forwarder; signed contracts with full Incoterms and rate cards; landed cost calculation; commercial invoices and Korean tax invoices; payment settlements evidenced by SWIFT MT103 history; warehouse in-and-out records; a freight audit report from an independent logistics auditor; and a company policy letter describing periodic benchmarking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The foreign parent's remittance for capital injection does not match the Korean entity's declared paid-in share capital or initial operational expenditure plan, showing split funding and unexplained intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Report or notification certificate with declared amount and purpose; board resolution setting out the amount of issued shares; a copy of the escrowed Foreign Investment Capital Account ledger; capital payment due report; fund flow chart; use-of-funds budget for GDP freight operations; copy of the investor's board resolution approving the capital increase; bank-to-bank remittance details showing the direct investor-to-target route; and a notarized statutory declaration confirming that no third-party funding intermediaries exist.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for a Korean Chusik Hoesa must be routed as a direct investor-to-company wire and reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before remittance. The foreign investor files a Foreign Investment Report with KOTRA or a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank; only then may the physical remittance be received into a dedicated Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account. The SWIFT MT103 should state the investor's name and account, the Korean corporation's registered name, the KOTRA or foreign investment notification number, and the FEIS purpose code for foreign direct investment equity acquisition. The bank will apply the exchange rate at value date, credit the KRW amount to the operational account and generate a Capital Payment Certificate. For capital verification, the statutory auditor or Korean certified accountant confirms that the paid-in capital equals the registered shares issued after the company's incorporation filing. No third-party funding, split remittances, or cash depot payment is acceptable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border freight and logistics disbursements, the Korean entity must pass payments through a domestic foreign exchange bank and a FEIS purpose code corresponding to freight and transportation charges. The clearing rail should be SWIFT MT103 for service payments and ancillary trade costs; a commercial letter of credit is preferred when the transaction involves physical purchase of temperature-controlled packaging, pharma cargo or equipment; documentary collection is acceptable for extended supplier payment terms. The bank requires a three-way match among the commercial invoice, customs declaration or airway bill, and the signed transport service contract. For domestic payments in KRW, Direct ACH using Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute bulk clearing is acceptable for local subcontractors, while SWIFT MT103 remains the foreign settlement rail. All outbound wires must record the underlying export or import declaration number and maintain audit trail connectivity to the FEIS report.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore US dollar and Korean won forward exchange contracts executed by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank for hedging legitimate freight receivables and payables, with maturity not exceeding the term of the underlying invoice plus 30 days and no contingent leverage.

KRW non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed by an overseas branch or offshore institution solely to hedge non-resident KRW profit or contractual exposure; NDFs are not a treasury tool for routine onshore onward purchases because settlement is in foreign currency and may fail the onshore real-demand test.

Cross-currency swaps and plain vanilla FX swaps restricted to converting a shareholder loan or capital account surplus into KRW for operational funding, with an underlying foreign-investment loan or trade-finance facility, counterparty limited to a top-tier domestic Korean bank, and no rollover beyond the loan term.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) package comprising statutory financial statements, business report, directors' report, auditor's report, AGM minutes and profit appropriation resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the Chusik Hoesa; copies retained at the registered office and made available to the National Tax Service (NTS) and external auditor upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held within three months after the close of each fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year end, no later than March 31; notice of convocation must be sent at least 14 days before the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the AGM or present financial statements are subject to administrative fines up to KRW 5,000,000 under the Korean Commercial Act; continued non-action may support court-ordered compulsory dissolution and liquidation; shareholder resolutions may be challenged on procedural grounds.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent certified public accountant's audit report on annual financial statements and appointment of external auditor under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS), Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA), DART if publicly listed, and NTS through the corporate tax return package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit report must be issued before the AGM and filed with the FSS/KICPA within three months after fiscal year end, i.e., March 31 for a December year-end; the auditor must be appointed at the AGM of the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If a mandatory auditee fails to appoint an auditor, the FSS may itself appoint the auditor and impose administrative sanctions; failure to file the audit report may expose the company to orders up to KRW 50,000,000 and criminal referral for materially false accounting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and local corporate surtax return, including tax reconciliation statement, financial statements, adjusted taxable income calculations and accumulated earnings tax computation where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS); the local corporate surtax is co-collected by the NTS and distributed to municipal and provincial tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the third month after the fiscal year end, i.e., March 31 for a December year-end; extension may be granted by the NTS but the payment due date is not extended
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file attracts a 20% additional tax on the unpaid or unreported amount, with fraudulent understatement subject to up to 40%; overdue balances accrue late-payment surcharge of approximately 0.025% per day (about 9.13% per annum); continued noncompliance enables NTS seizure, business registration cancellation and criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested enterprise annual business status report covering sales, employment, facility investment, shareholding changes and capital movements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) integrated foreign investment information system (GIS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the last day of February for a December fiscal year end; any change in foreign investment status, including share transfer, capital increase or decrease, relocation or representative change, must be reported within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or misreporting may result in a fine up to KRW 5,000,000 under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; KOTRA may issue correction orders; foreign investment protection, tax exemption status and dividend remittance approvals may be suspended until the report is cured.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual MFDS Good Distribution Practice (GDP) self-inspection report, license validity confirmation and change notification for pharmaceutical freight forwarding and logistics operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) and the relevant regional pharmaceutical regulatory authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the annual GDP inspection date or license anniversary; material changes to the licensed logistics site, responsible pharmacist or GDP procedures must be notified within 15 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative suspension or revocation of the GDP license and other MFDS regulatory authorization; administrative fines up to KRW 20,000,000; product recall orders for pharmaceuticals not handled in accordance with GDP; criminal liability under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act for falsified self-inspection or operational concealment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Register of shareholders and beneficial ownership validation report demonstrating that all share transfers, pledges and transfers of restrictions have been recorded and reconciled
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company itself at its registered office; foreign investor shareholding changes reported to KOTRA/GIS; copy provided to external auditor for substantive testing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Share transfers must be entered into the Register of Shareholders within 30 days of the transfer notice; annual validation must be completed before the AGM and signed by the representative director; for December year-end, the closing register should be fixed no later than the AGM date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A transferee cannot exercise shareholder rights against the company until register entry is completed; failure to maintain the statutory register triggers administrative fines up to KRW 5,000,000; an external auditor, if appointed, must issue a qualified opinion for incomplete statutory records; foreign investor dividend remittance may be blocked until the register and FIPA reports are consistent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax return and electronic tax invoice transmission for taxable supplies derived from freight forwarding, warehousing and ancillary pharmaceutical logistics services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic invoice platform and local tax office for VAT registration records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Semi-annual VAT returns: January 1 to June 30 filed by July 25; July 1 to December 31 filed by January 25; electronic tax invoices must be transmitted no later than the day after the supply date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid or unreported VAT triggers an additional tax of 10% of the unpaid VAT plus daily overdue surcharge of approximately 0.03%; late or omitted electronic tax invoices trigger penalties up to 1% of the supply value; repeated VAT nonfiling allows the NTS to cancel the business registration and compel closure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and the Framework Act on SMEs: (i) any Chusik Hoesa with total assets of at least KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,300,000) at the end of the preceding business year must obtain an independent CPA audit; (ii) a company with total assets between KRW 7,000,000,000 and KRW 12,000,000,000 becomes audit-mandated if it employs 100 or more regular employees or otherwise fails the SME size classification; (iii) any listed company on KRX, KOSDAQ or KONEX is always audit-mandated regardless of asset size; (iv) financial institutions, insurance companies, holding companies and other public-interest companies designated by the FSS are always audited; (v) where an MFDS GDP logistics license, foreign parent reporting or a lending covenant requires a certified audit, the statutory financial statements must be audited by a Korean certified public accountant. There is no standalone turnover trigger in the External Audit Act, but the FSS may designate an entity with annual revenue above KRW 10,000,000,000 as an audited company when necessary to protect creditors and public interest.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) applies to listed companies and certain public-interest entities; non-listed Chusik Hoesa entities may prepare statutory financial statements under K-GAAP (Korea Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) as prescribed by the Act on External Audit; tax returns reconcile K-GAAP or K-IFRS book income to taxable income under the Corporate Tax Act; all statutory accounts are prepared on an accrual basis in Korean Won and audited by a Korean certified public accountant; MFDS GDP logistics recordkeeping must satisfy pharmaceutical traceability rules in addition to accounting standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Korean Commercial Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a Chusik Hoesa must maintain an up-to-date Register of Shareholders at its registered office. Every share transfer must be notified to the company by the transferor, and the transferee obtains no enforceable shareholder rights until the transfer is entered in the register. The company must complete the register entry within 30 days of the transfer notice; any foreign investor shareholding change must also be reported to KOTRA/MOTIE through the integrated foreign investment information system within 30 days. Annually, before the AGM, the representative director must confirm the closing shareholder register, reconcile all transfers since the last register audit, and produce a UBO declaration for the external auditor and NTS filing package. The annual foreign-invested enterprise report is due by February 28 for each preceding calendar year. Failure to follow the 30-day reporting window invalidates corporate records, exposes the company to fines and prevents the shareholder from exercising voting, dividend and remittance rights until rectification.

Register of Corporate Bonds and Convertible Bonds
Financial Statements and Business Report Retention File

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 2,400 per year for a registered office, corporate secretarial agent or virtual office service in Seoul or major Korean business hubs
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 20,000 per year for a non-listed Korean stock corporation below or slightly above the statutory audit threshold; larger or public-interest auditees may face fees in the USD 30,000 - USD 80,000 range

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax on taxable income exceeding KRW 300,000,000,000; plus 10% local income tax surcharge yields an aggregate top marginal rate of 26.4%. Lower brackets are 9%, 19%, and 21%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign investment enterprises in Korea Free Economic Zones may enjoy a 100% corporate tax holiday for the first 3 years and 50% exemption for the next 2 years for qualifying FDI. R&D tax credits, employment credits, and special credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act are available to GDP pharma logistics operators that maintain documented clinical cold-chain innovation activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Payable Return, prescribed under Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act, filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic system; supplementary schedules include the International Transactions Report under Article 11 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return; quarterly corporate tax prepayments are required where first-half income exceeds the statutory threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; a calendar-year company files by March 31. The first-half interim prepayment for a calendar-year company is due by August 31.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate administrative identity: registration number, trade name, representative director, fiscal year, business place, and foreign investment enterprise registration details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose each non-resident shareholder and the percentage of Chusik Hoesa shares held. For treaty relief on eventual dividends, state the applicable residence country and confirm in the commentary box that the principal purpose of the entity is not treaty shopping.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from ISIC 5229 certified GDP logistics, freight forwarding, storage, clinical temperature-controlled transport, and ancillary invoicing services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separate Korean-source revenue from revenue attributable to any foreign permanent establishment. For international sea or air freight, apply the source rules of Corporate Tax Act Article 89 and evidence performance through bills of lading, waybills, Customs declarations, and temperature logs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible cost of services, wages, professional fees, leases, depreciation of cold-chain assets, GDP quality assurance, insurance, and regulatory costs; also non-deductible additions such as fines, political contributions, and excessive entertainment expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany costs paid to overseas freight affiliates may be disallowed if not at arm's length, if corresponding income is not recognized, or if no GDP operational substance is retained. Reconcile the International Transactions Report to remittance records and KRW conversion logs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determination of taxable income: adjusted gross revenue minus deductions, add-back of non-deductible expenses, carryforward tax losses, and application of tax holiday or free-zone deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a non-resident shareholder loan gives rise to interest deductions, apply the thin capitalization limitation and recharacterize excess interest as a hidden dividend. Attach a foreign tax credit schedule for any creditable DTA-compliant foreign taxes on Korean-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation: apply the progressive corporate tax brackets of 9%, 19%, 21%, and 24%, subtract R&D tax credits and other special credits, then deduct quarterly prepayments already paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not compute national corporate tax here. However, if retained earnings are capitalized above paid-in capital, reconcile any withholding tax on deemed constructive distributions separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cross-border related-party transactions and international tax matters: attach the International Transactions Report, transfer pricing Local File and Master File, and the tax treaty schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all dividends, interest, royalties, and intra-group logistics fees paid to non-residents. State the claimed withholding tax rate under the applicable Korea DTA and attach the non-resident's Tax Residency Certificate, proof of beneficial ownership, board minutes, and equity ownership details. Without these, Korea will withhold at the statutory 22% composite rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Representative director's declaration that the return, schedules, and attachments are complete and accurate; HomeTax electronic signature and payment summary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Chusik Hoesa under non-resident control, the Korean representative director assumes criminal responsibility for false filing. A non-resident beneficial owner cannot disclaim the filing exposure of the domestic entity, and the director may be personally liable for acts performed in the name of the company.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing exposes the taxpayer to an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax where the return is filed after the legal deadline, increasing to 40% where the understatement is fraudulent. Unpaid tax accrues a daily late payment surcharge of 0.022%. Criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may lead to imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to 5 times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national corporate income tax withholding plus 10% local income tax surcharge on the national tax, producing a composite 22% statutory withholding rate on cash dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders that do not obtain treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit to the National Tax Service: an official Tax Residency Certificate issued by the treaty country; a signed Application for Tax Reduction or Exemption under the Tax Treaty; proof of beneficial ownership; shareholding percentage and holding-period evidence; and substance documentation such as employees, board minutes, bank accounts, and business premises in the residence state. Korea applies the principal purpose test under the OECD MLI and denies treaty benefits if a main purpose of the structure is treaty shopping. Reduced withholding is applied only after NTS acceptance or through a timely refund claim.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates are 20% national tax plus 2% local surcharge for both interest and royalties, for a composite 22%. Treaty rates generally range from 10% to 15% for interest and royalties. For dividends, treaty rates typically fall between 5% and 15% depending on shareholding level and holding-period conditions. Arm's-length freight service income is not subject to withholding, but payments labeled as management, marketing, or distribution fees may be recharacterized as royalty or dividend under anti-abuse rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Korea requires contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation where cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 10,000,000,000 per relevant transaction category, or where the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds KRW 100,000,000,000 and aggregate cross-border intercompany transactions exceed KRW 50,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulation regime, but substance governs treaty access through the beneficial ownership and principal purpose tests. The Korean Chusik Hoesa must demonstrate that board meetings, cold-chain freight operations, personnel, bank accounts, invoices, and core income-generating activities are performed or located in Korea. If the entity is a letter-box company and management is abroad, Korea may disregard the corporate shell, impute profits to the actual owner, and treat remittances as distributable dividends subject to withholding.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fabricated GDP Freight Expenses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The corporation issues invoices for certified pharmaceutical GDP transportation without temperature-monitoring records, delivery proofs, MFDS GDP registration, or actual physical handling, and files false deductible expense entries to shift profit out of Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, a person who evades tax by fraudulent or unjust means is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine not exceeding 5 times the evaded tax. The Framework Act on National Taxes additionally imposes a 40% unfaithful-return additional tax. If the false expenses are linked to money laundering, the Proceeds of Crime Act adds asset forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director who signs the false return loses the liability shield: he or she is jointly and severally liable for the corporation's tax and unpaid withholding tax under Article 39 of the National Tax Collection Act. Personal assets may be reached through civil restitution in shareholder derivative actions and creditors' direct suits. The director may be classified as a high-amount abusive tax delinquent, resulting in travel bans, public blacklisting, asset seizures, and criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing / Thin Capitalization and False Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The subsidiary pays non-arm's-length fees to a non-resident affiliate in a zero-tax jurisdiction for quality-assurance coordination while performing all core pharmacy GDP freight operations itself. It also services non-resident shareholder loans at materially below-market interest rates and submits fabricated CUP benchmarks in the Local File.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 10 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs permits the NTS to re-determine taxable income using the arm's length standard, with a correlative adjustment under Article 14. The unpaid tax is increased by a 20%-40% unfaithful-return penalty under Article 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. Knowingly false transfer-pricing documentation may be referred for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the false Local File and transfer-pricing declaration may be sued for damages under Article 399 of the Commercial Act. The court may pierce the corporate veil where the company is a mere instrumentality, leaving directors liable for adjusted tax, interest, and penalties. In serious cases, personal bank accounts and securities are seized, exit from Korea is prohibited until tax clearance, and conviction carries imprisonment of up to 5 years plus fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Shopping Beneficial Ownership Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-resident shareholders establish the Korean Chusik Hoesa as a letter-box holding company with no board meetings, no employees, no leased cold-chain storage, and no core income-generating activities. Profits are streamed through the entity solely as a conduit to claim the reduced DTA dividend rate and to avoid Korean withholding tax on dividends or royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS applies the principal purpose test under Article 7 of the OECD MLI as incorporated into Korea's tax conventions, denies treaty benefits, and recharacterizes remittances as Korean-source dividends subject to 22% withholding. The Framework Act on National Taxes Article 14 and the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs Article 12 authorize substance-over-form and treaty-abuse adjustments. A mandatory 40% false-return penalty applies, and failure to withhold and remit triggers independent penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The nominee director is stripped of the corporate veil because he or she exercised no independent judgment. As the responsible withholding agent, the director is personally liable for the 22% withholding deficiency. Courts may order civil restitution disgorging all fees received for the conduit arrangement, the director's travel is restricted under the National Tax Collection Act blacklist regime, and intentional non-withholding of non-resident tax carries criminal imprisonment of up to 3 years.
